newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strauss-Kahn wants quick pact solution if possible.
newsitem.headline: Strauss-Kahn wants quick pact solution if possible.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Wednesday he wanted a quick solution if possible to a dispute over an EU stability pact limiting budget deficits under monetary union.
"If we can move forward quickly it is obviously better. No-one wants to drag things out just for the sake of it," he told reporters after cabinet meeting.

He had been asked whether it was true that the French government could sign up to the stability pact at an EU Amsterdam summit on June 16 and 17 without waiting for Prime Minister Lionel Jospin to make his keynote policy speech to parliament, expected on June 19.
"The question is to know how we can obtain the balance we are seeking," he said.
He added that as regards an agreement "the sooner the better".
Strauss-Kahn also said the possibility of holding an emergency European finance ministers meeting in Amsterdam on Sunday, June 15, ahead of the summit "is not ruled out".

France's new Socialist-led government, which swept to power in a June 1 election upset, is seeking a better balance in Europe between budget discipline and price stability on one hand and the need for growth and jobs on the other.
